messages:
alex: FYI running into typers failing on our sample app with the async Python SDK after the autogen update

alex: failing case is weird: generator produced Optional[Union[List[WidgetV1], Tuple[WidgetV2, ...]]] for the same response field depending on oneOf heuristics

alex: snippet from generated models:```python
class WidgetsResp(BaseModel):
    payload: Optional[Union[List[WidgetV1], Tuple[WidgetV2, ...]]] = None
```

priya: ugh tuple vs list mix is a new one. mypy/pyright both get confused especially with comprehensions and chained calls

josh: how are you consuming it in the sample app?

alex: sample:```python
resp = await client.fetch_widgets()
flat = [w for coll in (resp.payload or []) for w in coll]
print(len(flat))
```

alex: mypy error: "Item "None" of "Optional[Union[List[WidgetV1], Tuple[WidgetV2, ...]]]" has no attribute "__iter__"" and then downstream code expects .id attribute on items but types are inconsistent

priya: two problems: (1) union-of-collections instead of collection-of-union, (2) mixing list/tuple makes inference brittle. Autogen heuristics should normalize array schemas to the same container type and prefer List[Union[...]]

josh: agreed. also spotted that our docs sample app (examples/async/sample_widgets.py) does `for w in resp.payload:` which silently type-checks in pyright in our local env but fails in CI with mypy pinned older version

alex: created a tiny repro repo and ran both mypy and pyright matrix locally. Repro shows pyright accepts it leniently but mypy flags errors depending on strictness settings

dev-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/420 - "autogen: inconsistent container types in array unions cause typing failures"

priya: short-term mitigation ideas: (a) generator emits Optional[List[Union[A,B]]] when multiple item schemas found, (b) add a config option `normalize_array_unions: bool` default true, (c) emit a compat alias Type: `WidgetsPayload = List[Union[WidgetV1, WidgetV2]]` and keep the original spec-shaped type as a private symbol with # type: ignore in the public API

josh: from SDK maintenance POV, adding a default that improves typing (normalize_array_unions=true) is acceptable but we need to note this in changelog and provide upgrade guide. Some users might rely on precise generated types for validators but runtime validation unchanged

priya: another related annoyance: sync vs async client return typing mismatch. We generate `Iterable[Widget]` for sync and `AsyncIterator[Widget]` for async. That breaks shared utility functions that assume a plain `Iterable`. Suggest we introduce a shared Protocol `SupportsIter[T]` or make both return `Sequence[T]` where appropriate

alex: could also supply thin adapters in the SDK: `to_sync_iterable()` helpers around async iterators for sample apps and docs so onboarding is smoother

josh: agree. Add a short note in onboarding doc: "If you use generated models, prefer iterating with `for item in (resp.payload or [])` or cast to List[Union[...]] to satisfy mypy. We'll ship generator change to make this unnecessary soon."

ci-bot: CI job created: typing-matrix/199200 - runs mypy 0.991, mypy 1.2, pyright latest

alex: I'm going to open a PR with: repro tests, generator fix (normalize_array_unions), and a tiny docs update. Assigning to @priya to review typing changes

priya: will review. can you include unit tests that assert generated stub text contains "List[Union" and that mypy passes on the generated package? That will prevent regressions

alex: yep. I'll also add a migration note in release notes and an example transform snippet for users who want to keep the old shape

josh: thanks. tagging #devex and #dev-sdks so folks who hit onboarding errors can find the issue

alex: link to issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/420

priya: nice work reproing this quickly. once PR lands we should update sample apps in examples/ to the new generated types and run the onboarding quickstart to verify no docs bitrot

alex: will follow up with PR link shortly

josh: :thumbsup:
